Any two blocks meet in 0 or 2 points, so no 5-set contains two blocks. Counting pairs (5-set, block inside it) gives 14·4 = 56, which equals the number of 5-sets, so every 5-set F contains exactly one block B = F∖{w}.

In a cyclic order of F, the windows avoiding w are two consecutive triples. Both lie in B, and each triple's only edge is B, so they cannot receive distinct edges. Hence there is no Berge-C₅³ on F, and n = 8 fails. The proposal is correct here.
